research_goal: To analyze Type Ia supernova light curves by integrating peak magnitude, decay rate, and observational evidence of progenitor systems, enabling comparative studies across datasets and supporting model validation in cosmology.

information_needs.need_name: peak magnitude and associated filter band
information_needs.reason: Critical for standardizing luminosity measurements and comparing brightness across surveys; essential for cosmological distance estimation.

information_needs.need_name: decay rate (e.g., delta m15, stretch factor)
information_needs.reason: Determines the shape of the light curve and is used to classify SN Ia and correct for intrinsic brightness variations.
Supports model validation by linking observed light curves to physical origins (e.g., double-degenerate vs. single-degenerate).
Helps assess environmental effects on SN Ia properties and enables accurate K-correction and cosmological modeling.
Enables cross-calibration between surveys and identification of systematic biases due to instrumental response or bandpass differences.

information_needs.need_name: light curve fit parameters and residuals
information_needs.reason: Provides context for how peak magnitude and decay rate were derived, allowing assessment of data quality and fitting methodology.

information_needs.need_name: metadata on data provenance and confidence
information_needs.reason: Ensures traceability and reliability of extracted values, especially when multiple sources report conflicting results.

dynamic_tables.description: Extracts key photometric properties of Type Ia supernovae including peak magnitude and decay rate, linked to specific observations and filters.

fields.name: supernova_name
fields.description: Unique identifier for the supernova (e.g., SN 2011fe, PS1-13bnr)

fields.name: redshift
fields.description: Cosmological redshift measured from spectroscopic data; used for K-correction and distance modulus calculation

fields.name: peak_magnitude
fields.description: Apparent magnitude at maximum brightness; must be reported in a standard filter band

fields.name: filter_band
fields.description: Photometric band used (e.g., B, V, g, r, i); critical for consistency across surveys

fields.name: decay_rate
fields.description: Rate of decline in brightness after peak; commonly expressed as delta m15 (mag/100 days) or stretch factor

fields.name: observation_telescope
fields.description: Telescope used for photometric observations (e.g., Keck, LSST, Hubble)

fields.name: host_galaxy_type
fields.description: Morphological classification of host galaxy (e.g., spiral, elliptical, irregular)

dynamic_tables.description: Captures observational and theoretical support for proposed progenitor models of each supernova.

fields.name: supernova_name
fields.description: Reference to the supernova being analyzed

fields.name: progenitor_model
fields.description: Proposed origin scenario: e.g., 'double-degenerate', 'single-degenerate', 'hybrid', 'no clear evidence'

dynamic_tables.description: Records details about light curve fitting procedures, including parameters, residuals, and goodness-of-fit metrics.

fields.name: supernova_name
fields.description: Target supernova for which light curve was fitted

fields.name: fit_method
fields.description: Name of fitting algorithm or model used (e.g., SALT2, MLCS2k2, SiFTO)

fields.name: fit_parameters
fields.description: List of fitted parameters (e.g., amplitude, time of peak, stretch, color excess)

fields.name: residual_std_dev
fields.description: Standard deviation of residuals from the best-fit model; indicates fit quality

fields.name: chi_squared
fields.description: Chi-squared value indicating statistical fit quality

quality_rules: All extracted values must be directly traceable to a verifiable source (paper, table, figure, or supplementary material).
Evidence_text must include a verbatim excerpt or caption that supports the claim.
Confidence scores must reflect data quality and source reliability; no hallucinated or assumed values allowed.
When multiple sources report conflicting values for the same metric and supernova, the discrepancy must be recorded in the cross_survey_comparisons table.
Filter band and redshift must be consistent with published standards; if uncertain, flag with 'uncertain' in evidence_text.
Do not infer or extrapolate missing values; use null if information is unavailable.
Record-level provenance fields are stored outside dynamic table fields and must not be duplicated.
Task-specific fields omitted by the schema planner were restored in other_required_fields.
missing_data_policy: Use null for missing information; do not fabricate values.
